  "text": "On Thursday, Martin brought his wife’s shoes to the repair shop. The heel had come loose from one, and she had put them by the front door in February.

The man behind the counter spread a cloth before taking them.

“Both heels?”

“Just the left, I think.”

“Better to do the pair. Otherwise she’ll notice the difference.”

Martin looked at the shelves behind him. Shoes stood in brown paper bags, their toes showing.

“All right,” he said.

The man wrote on a ticket and pushed it across.

“Tuesday.”

Outside, Martin folded the ticket into his wallet. He had other errands, but the list was on the kitchen table. He went to the bakery and bought two rolls.

On Tuesday it rained. He waited until Wednesday, then felt foolish for having waited.

The repairer remembered the shoes.

“Came up nicely,” he said, turning one so Martin could see the heel. “Good leather. Worth looking after.”

At home, Martin left the bag on a chair while he put away his shopping. He had bought milk, washing powder and a jar of mustard he already had.

He took the shoes upstairs. Their place in the wardrobe was still there, beside her winter boots.

Before putting them away, he peeled the price label from the sole. It resisted, leaving a small white patch. He rubbed it with his thumb, then fetched a damp cloth from the bathroom.

He left the shoes out to dry on a sheet of newspaper. In the morning he moved them off the paper before opening the wardrobe."
